patch_resolves_note: The authoritative fixed commit extends `regsize_map_32` and `regsize_map_64` with four 16-byte BND entries. On the original `BNDLDXrm` witness path, `printMemReference()` still executes, but it now reaches the fallback guard with `MI->op1_size` already set to 16, so the stale `MI->x86opsize` byte is never copied into `MI->op1_size` and the later sink reads a defined byte.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `printMemReference()` can fall back to `MI->op1_size = MI->x86opsize`, the earlier BND register-operand path must already have established a nonzero `MI->op1_size` for this instruction.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the vulnerable `BNDLDXrm` witness path, the missing BND entries in `regsize_map_32` leave `MI->op1_size` at 0 when `printMemReference()` evaluates `if (MI->op1_size == 0)`. The fixed commit appends 16-byte BND widths, so the same path reaches this guard with `MI->op1_size` already set and the fallback copy is no longer needed.

nodes.description: At the sanitizer sink, the left operand of `if (MI->op1_size == 0 && reg)` reads the one-byte `MI->op1_size` field after the fallback copy path.
Immediately after `printMemReference()` executes `MI->op1_size = MI->x86opsize`, the destination byte `MI->op1_size` is still uninitialized on the witness path.

edges.relation: The same `MI->op1_size` field examined by the fallback guard is the destination field overwritten one statement later by `MI->op1_size = MI->x86opsize`.
The same `MI->op1_size` byte written by the fallback copy in `printMemReference()` is the byte later consumed at the `X86_Intel_printInst()` sink.
